intro: Lesson 108: Measuring resistance: circuit symbols, ammeters and voltmeters. To understand how to set up a circuit with an ammeter and voltmeter to find resistance

head: Component
What it does
rows: resistance changes with light and temperature

questions.q: Readings: 4.5 V and 0.15 A. Resistance? [2 marks]
questions.model: Formula: R = V ÷ I. Substitute: 4.5 ÷ 0.15. Calculate: 30. Unit: Ω.

questions.q: From the graph, what is the resistance of the resistor?
Why is the I-V graph a straight line through the origin?
questions.a: Current is proportional to voltage (constant resistance).

questions.q: Core: Draw the circuit diagram to measure a resistor's resistance with an ammeter, voltmeter, variable resistor and cell. Then calculate R from four readings (portal worksheet).
questions.a: Ammeter in series, voltmeter across the resistor; R values all about 20 Ω; mean 20 Ω.
questions.model: Teacher draws it first: cell, switch, variable resistor, ammeter in one loop with the resistor; voltmeter on a parallel branch across the resistor.

questions.q: Extend: Describe how to investigate the I-V characteristics of a filament lamp. [4 marks] Use the portal response box.
questions.a: Circuit with ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel (1); vary voltage with variable resistor (1); record pairs of V and I (1); reverse the supply and repeat, plot I against V (1).

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why a filament lamp's I-V graph curves.
questions.a: As current increases, the filament heats up and its resistance increases, so current rises less steeply.

questions.q: Big question: how do you measure resistance?
questions.a: Measure V across and I through the component, then R = V ÷ I.
